clue.text: Unlikely winners don't cook enough eggs on a regular basis

parts.note: to underdo food is to cook it too little

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, every second one of the word eggs

explanation.surface: A grumble about someone who skimps on the cooking of a breakfast of eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on a regular basis' picks the second and fourth letters of 'eggs', GS.
explanation.definitionFit: Those not expected to triumph in a contest are the ones tipped to lose, so their wins come as surprises.

clue.text: A scene with liberal drink supply? Virgin territory, in more ways than one

definitions.text: Virgin territory, in more ways than one

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, flexibly, so the letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: A tourist brochure praising a party spot where alcohol flows freely, then hinting at untouched land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a noun but is the adverb 'supply' (in a supple way), the anagram signal, rearranging A SCENE, L and DRINK. Someone who 'necks' drinks might be a necker, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caribbean isle is owned by Richard Branson, founder of the Virgin group, and is also unspoilt, pristine land.

clue.text: Two short names for a man or woman

parts.note: the first of two brief first names is Eve
the second brief first name is Lyn, a short form of Lynette

explanation.surface: A baby-naming tip: two brief names make one that suits either sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two short names' supplies both halves, EVE and LYN. The name is borne by men (Evelyn Waugh) and women alike.
explanation.definitionFit: This first name is given to people of either sex, so it can stand for a man or a woman.

clue.text: See 11
One that's spotted if Nigel Farage is upset, not representing Ealing

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters of the phrase are scrambled
not representing removes the letters of the London borough from the scrambled pool

parts.note: Ealing is a borough of west London, here a constituency the politician does not represent

explanation.surface: Politics: something gets noticed if Nigel Farage is put out at not being the MP for Ealing.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the letters of IF NIGEL FARAGE, once those of EALING are taken away, rearrange to the answer. Nigel Farage is a British Brexit-campaigning politician; Ealing is a west London borough.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall African animal has a patterned, blotched coat, so it is a creature covered in spots.

clue.text: Very small chap, one that goes ballistic

parts.note: minute means tiny
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A tiny fellow with a short temper who flies into rages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes ballistic' suggests losing one's temper, but it means a ballistic missile.
explanation.definitionFit: Minuteman is the name of a US intercontinental ballistic missile, so it literally goes ballistic.

clue.text: Ring newspaper editor about home with trees damaged by loose, uneven bits of Sopwith Camel

indicators.note: loose means set free, so the selected letters move into a new order
uneven means odd-numbered, so take the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O
FT is the Financial Times
H is short for home, as in sports fixtures
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor; about here just means close by, the editor standing next to home

indicators.note: damaged signals the letters are knocked out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: A tangled order to phone an editor about a house whose trees were hit by a Sopwith Camel biplane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Camel' looks like part of the plane's name, but it is the definition. The Sopwith Camel was a First World War fighter biplane; 'loose' and 'damaged' are the two anagram signals.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal is nicknamed this because it carries people and goods across sandy wastes as a boat crosses the sea.

clue.text: Where kids have fun seeing Mary's polo game

indicators.note: game in the sense of lame or crooked, so the letters are put out of shape

explanation.surface: Children enjoy themselves watching Mary play polo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like the sport, but it is the adjective meaning lame, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: These are rooms in a home set aside for children's toys and games.

clue.text: Timid people include 'hard left' Frenchman

indicators.note: include means the timid people take a letter in among them

parts.note: timid people are mice, as in 'are you a man or a mouse?'
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Shy folk welcome a far-left political Frenchman into their midst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard left' reads as a political phrase but splits into H and L, the first going inside MICE, the second following.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common French male first name, the counterpart of Michael.

clue.text: Credit must be taken by fast bowlers!!

indicators.note: taken by means held within, so credit goes inside the bowlers

parts.note: seamers are quick cricket bowlers who make the ball move off its seam
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator's excited cry that the quick bowlers deserve their praise.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the pair of exclamation marks, not a word. In cricket, seamers are medium to fast bowlers.
explanation.definitionFit: Printers and journalists call an exclamation mark a screamer, so two of them are a pair of these.

clue.text: For the Fallen, twice read: 28 rhyming words

definitions.text: For the Fallen, twice read: 28 rhyming words

parts.words: For the Fallen, twice read: 28 rhyming words
parts.note: the nursery-rhyme egg who had a great fall, his two-word name both rhyming with the answer to 28

explanation.surface: Reads like a note on Binyon's war poem For the Fallen, read twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For the Fallen' is a famous remembrance poem, but here points to the nursery-rhyme egg who had a great fall; both halves of the name rhyme with 28's answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery-rhyme character sat on a wall and had a great fall, and both words of the name rhyme.

clue.text: Badly stymied and frustrated, you initially make clear

indicators.note: badly signals the letters are put together wrongly, in a new order
initially picks the opening letters of the two words before it

explanation.surface: Someone thwarted and annoyed asks you to explain things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives F and Y from 'frustrated' and 'you'; 'Badly' rearranges them with STYMIED.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip away the mystery from something is to explain it and make it understandable.

clue.text: Unwilling to heed content of idea FT originated

indicators.note: the content is what is held inside the words, the letters running across them

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to listen to an idea from the Financial Times.
explanation.walkthrough: FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Being deaf to advice is a figurative way of refusing to listen to it.

clue.text: Daughter being sinful with the same bold action

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in genealogy
erring means straying from virtue
do is short for ditto, meaning the same

explanation.surface: A daughter misbehaves in exactly the same daring way as before.
explanation.definitionFit: This old-fashioned phrase means heroic, daring deeds.

clue.text: Bloomer by model, eating hot carrageen

indicators.note: eating means the pair take a letter inside them
by means next to, placing the model after the flower

parts.note: a bloomer is something that blooms, here the iris flower
Kate Moss is a famous fashion model
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A gaffe by a model while eating something spicy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a blunder or loaf, but means a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrageen is a red seaweed of Atlantic coasts, also known by this name.

clue.text: Fool goes in to see yes-men?

parts.note: an ass is a fool
enters means goes in

explanation.surface: A clown walks in to visit the sycophants.
explanation.definitionFit: People who agree to everything say yes, so they are those who give their agreement.

clue.text: Honey Bee, say?

definitions.meaning: the Latin word for honey, used in pharmacy
Spice Girl ... B, whose initial sounds like the insect, so this is a first name like hers

explanation.surface: Reads like a query about a honey bee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Honey Bee' looks like one phrase but splits into two definitions. Mel B is a member of the British pop group the Spice Girls.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for honey, also the first name of the singer known as Mel B.

clue.text: Computer's current backup

indicators.note: read as back up, going upwards in a down entry, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a current is a flowing river, here the Cam of Cambridge

explanation.surface: A note about a computer's present data backup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backup' suggests a data copy, but it is 'back up', a reversal in a down clue. The Cam is the river at Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple's personal computer line is known by this short name.

clue.text: Cut off short run with a bounding stride

indicators.note: short means the word is cut back by its last letter

parts.note: to lope is to run with long, easy strides

explanation.surface: A sprinter is stopped short while running with long strides.
explanation.definitionFit: To lop a branch is to chop it off.

clue.text: Sloth's a regret, when returning to large area of land

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the ai is a three-toed sloth, plus the S of the possessive
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Laziness is a cause of remorse once it comes home to roost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sloth' looks like the deadly sin but is the animal, the ai.
explanation.definitionFit: Europe and Asia together form one combined landmass, a vast area of land.

clue.text: How one man composed capriciously

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Describes how a man wrote his music on impulse.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting on impulse, without a plan, is the same as acting capriciously.

clue.text: Clarkson as presenter, originally for Top Gear

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: Jeremy Clarkson as the original presenter of the TV car show Top Gear.
explanation.walkthrough: Top Gear is a BBC motoring show once fronted by Jeremy Clarkson, but here means headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing worn on the head is gear for the top of the body, such as a peaked hat.

clue.text: Punishing a couple in Russia

indicators.note: in places the couple inside the country's abbreviation

parts.note: RUS is the international abbreviation for Russia
a duo is a couple

explanation.surface: Something harsh happens to a pair in Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: A punishing schedule is a gruelling, very demanding one.

clue.text: Spots royal being more reckless

parts.note: a rash is an outbreak of spots
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A royal person is seen with blemishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spots' suggests sees, but means skin blemishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Rash means hasty and careless, and this is its comparative form.

clue.text: Camel's broken spirit

indicators.note: broken means smashed apart, so the letters are reassembled differently

explanation.surface: A camel whose will has been broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' suggests morale, but is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: This Mexican distilled liquor is made from agave, a type of spirit.

clue.text: Hot water off the south coast, after temperature rises by 4 degrees?

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means moving upwards, here four places

parts.note: the Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight and the English south coast

explanation.surface: A weather report on sea temperatures climbing off England's south coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The Solent is the channel between the Isle of Wight and Hampshire. 'Hot' looks like weather, but is slang for stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot is slang for goods recently taken illegally, and so hard to sell.

clue.text: See 2
Promote short clue within contrary setting

indicators.note: within means the shortened clue sits inside the other word

parts.note: adverse means contrary, as in adverse winds

indicators.note: short means the word is cut back by its final letter

parts.note: a tip is a clue or hint

explanation.surface: A setter boosts a brief hint inside an awkward puzzle setting.
explanation.definitionFit: To publicise a product is to push or promote it.

clue.text: Idiot that's wrecked my punt

indicators.note: wrecked means smashed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fool who has wrecked the speaker's punt.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a Scottish and northern British slang word for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a foolish or incompetent person.

clue.text: Everybody in Hackney perhaps needs to instruct youth about love

parts.note: to coach is to instruct

indicators.note: about means going round, the youth surrounding love

parts.note: a lad is a youth
O is zero, love in tennis

explanation.surface: A community in an East London borough needs to teach youngsters about love.
explanation.walkthrough: Hackney looks like the London borough, but a hackney is a horse-drawn carriage for hire.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach carrying a full load holds everyone in it; a hackney carriage is one kind of coach.

clue.text: See 7
Surprisingly pleased about a new seaside amenity

indicators.note: about means surrounding, the jumbled letters going round the rest
surprisingly signals an unexpected arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Someone is unexpectedly delighted by a fresh seaside facility.
explanation.definitionFit: A promenade along the seafront is a public walkway that is a typical seaside feature.
